question: Should earliest-layer exact-path ownership, with only provably monotonic tools.allow and tools.deny exceptions, become OpenClaw's supported managed-configuration authority model?
rationale: Tests and lifecycle proof can validate an implementation, but they cannot decide whether this precedence and security model should become the permanent product contract.

options.title: Accept narrow V1
options.body: Approve the startup-only immutable model and land the RFC only when the linked implementation matches the accepted contract.

options.title: Revise authority rules
options.body: Keep both drafts open and request specific changes to precedence, monotonic exceptions, diagnostics, or compatibility behavior.

options.title: Decline core composition
options.body: Leave multi-source composition in host integrations rather than establishing a core managed-configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow V1
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only immutable model and land the RFC only when the linked implementation matches the accepted contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows explicit involvement, and the decision spans core product, compatibility, and security direction.
